text:
Nikita Kucherov told the Lightning at the end of October that he won't re-sign and wants a trade (the Associated Press broke it), and while general manager Julien BriseBois has said he has no intention of moving him, the rumor mill has spent the week shipping him everywhere from Toronto to Dallas. Nothing about his game looks distracted. He had six points in two games this week, including a hat trick against Buffalo, and has 28 points in 19 games for a Tampa team that keeps winning at home.

The process is real, and so is a little luck. Tampa has scored 7.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice; his own finishing is normal (8 goals on 6.6 expected). Our talent range has him around 4.5 points per 60; he's at 4.2, so if anything there's room.

Evolving-Hockey rated him the second most valuable forward in the league last season, with the usual caveat that he gives some back defensively. Whatever the Lightning decide, the player on the block is the reigning Hart Trophy winner, and he's playing like it.
headline: Asking out, still putting up points
